html:
MeerKAT is a radio telescope of 64 dish antennas in the Karoo of the Northern Cape, South Africa, inaugurated in 2018. It is one of the most sensitive radio telescopes in the world.

In 2003 South Africa bid to host the Square Kilometre Array (SKA), a planned giant radio telescope. MeerKAT began as a local array to show it could be done, and to train African engineers and scientists. In 2012 the SKA was split between South Africa and Australia, and MeerKAT will become part of the South African half.

The dry, empty Karoo is protected by law from radio noise, which is why the site was chosen. MeerKAT's results include a sharp radio image of the centre of the Milky Way and the discovery of huge radio bubbles there, as well as new pulsars and distant galaxies. It has made South Africa a centre of radio astronomy.
